clue.text: Damned awful dogs set on journalist

parts.note: curs are mongrels, dogs of the nasty, worthless sort
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: Someone curses the vicious dogs that were set on a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set on' is a down-clue habit used here in an across: the dogs come first, then the journalist after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something damned has been condemned, put under a curse.

clue.text: Accepted practice in America failing people ultimately

parts.note: USA is the familiar abbreviation for the United States of America

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words failing and people

explanation.surface: A custom in the United States is dying out because people no longer keep it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' covers both 'failing' and 'people', giving G and E after USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: established custom or convention, the way things are normally done.

clue.text: Herd suffering with sleet to be put in barn?

indicators.note: a herd suffering in sleet is battered about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cattle suffering in the sleet need to be brought indoors into the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges HERD and SLEET together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: animals housed in a barn are protected from the weather, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stupid person presenting pudding to the Queen

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A dim-witted guest offers a homemade pudding to Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUM DUFF is a traditional British steamed pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dimwit or incompetent, especially an inept old fellow.

clue.text: Plants gone wild within slanted line

indicators.note: within says the rearranged letters sit inside the line

parts.note: bias is a diagonal line across the grain of fabric

indicators.note: gone wild means these letters are let loose into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener's plants have run riot across a sloping border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slanted line' is dressmaking's bias, cut across the grain; 'wild' makes EGON, which sits 'within' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are flowering garden and house plants with showy blooms.

clue.text: Bad forefathers I worked out to be group of similar type

indicators.note: worked out means the letters are puzzled over and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Someone works out that their ancestors were a bad lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges all of BAD FOREFATHERS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: from the proverb that such creatures flock together, meaning people of the same kind.

clue.text: Good indoor workers maybe heading off to be field workers

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: cleaners are an example of workers indoors, hence maybe

explanation.surface: Good domestic staff set off outdoors to work the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags that cleaners are only one kind of indoor worker; 'heading off' leaves LEANERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: they gather leftover grain from fields after harvest.

clue.text: Some preventing upset with word of denial

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are read from bottom to top
Some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Preventing someone from being upset takes a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes REVEN from inside 'preventing', and 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an emphatic no, denying something will ever happen.

clue.text: Get right into a seat — with legs thus?

indicators.note: into says the right letter is placed inside the seat

parts.note: a staddle is a supporting base or frame, such as the stone seat on which a haystack rests

explanation.surface: Instructions for mounting: get properly into the saddle, legs either side.
explanation.walkthrough: The seat everyone expects is SADDLE, which leaves a T unexplained; STADDLE, a stone base for a stack, is the obscure seat that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: sitting with one leg each side of something, as a rider does.

clue.text: Tradesfolk start to supply drinks for church

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the word supply

parts.note: ales are beers, so drinks
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Traders begin supplying drinks to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is a common crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a company's team of salespeople, the people who trade its goods.

clue.text: Prohibit nothing following check

indicators.note: following says nothing comes after the check

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A ban comes into force after an inspection finds nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the O after VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to forbid or block, as a president may block a bill.

clue.text: Dogs, about fifty — they have arrived in new homes

definitions.text: they have arrived in new homes

indicators.note: about means the dogs go round the fifty

parts.note: setters are gun dogs
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: About fifty dogs have been rehomed with new owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places L inside SETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: colonists who have moved to make their homes in a new land.

clue.text: Usual line taken by operatic woman

indicators.note: taken by means the line is held by the woman, following her name

parts.note: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: An opera singer delivers the line in her customary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' sets L after NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ordinary, typical, what is standard.

clue.text: Box no longer wanted with side missing

indicators.note: a side is a compass point such as east, so its letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: spare means surplus, not needed any more

explanation.surface: A spare box with one side gone is now useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with side missing' drops E (east) from SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Map finally needs east-west indication? That is obvious!

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word map

parts.note: lines of latitude run east to west across a map

explanation.surface: A map needs an east-west line marked on it, and that is plainly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a trite remark, something so obvious it hardly needed saying.

clue.text: Players supporting children without parents?

parts.note: if you are for something, you support it
wards are children placed in a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A team's players back orphaned children as a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Wards may have living parents, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: attackers in football, rugby or hockey teams.

clue.text: Stylish and unusual tea chest seen around India

indicators.note: seen around means the rearranged letters wrap around the letter
unusual means the letters are made strange, put in a new order

parts.note: India is I in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An unusual, stylish tea chest has been spotted travelling around India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TEA CHEST, which is 'seen around' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: concerned with beauty and good taste, so tasteful and stylish.

clue.text: Author has month with priest, someone very holy

parts.note: NOV is short for November
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: A writer spends a month with a priest and a saintly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a writer of fiction, specifically long-form stories.

clue.text: Worker so very loud? Keep away!

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A worker is so noisy that people tell them to stay away.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a warning not to touch or interfere.

clue.text: The lady died in Slough

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: A woman died in Slough, the English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town; it is the verb, as a snake sloughs its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cast off or discard, as a snake does its skin.

clue.text: Composer in pub having drink half-heartedly

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a room in one

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters, half the heart, is removed

parts.note: beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A composer sits in the pub nursing a drink without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one E from the middle of BEER, leaving BER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Samuel, the American who wrote the Adagio for Strings.

clue.text: Criminal at sea getting cross at stern of ship

indicators.note: a ship's stern is its rear, so the last letter of the word ship

parts.note: irate means angry, cross

explanation.surface: A criminal at sea becomes angry at the back of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sea robber who attacks ships.

clue.text: First letter to the Corinthians

parts.note: looks like Paul's epistle in the Bible, but the Corinthians were Greek, so it asks for the opening character of their writing system

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase calls up St Paul's First Epistle to the Corinthians; it really asks for the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: it heads the Greek alphabet, used by ancient Corinth.

clue.text: Botswana — the magician comes with this imprecation

indicators.note: comes with this says the words carry the answer within them, spanning the gaps

explanation.surface: A conjuror from Botswana arrives uttering a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in 'Botswana' and ends in 'magician'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal curse, or something cursed and detested.

clue.text: Fellow on journey finds fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the fellow above the journey

parts.note: man means a fellow
a go can be a trip or turn, so a journey

explanation.surface: A man on his travels discovers fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Something to eat and drink quietly

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink
P, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat something and sip a drink quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cut of beef from the hindquarters, eaten as steak.

clue.text: Favoured worker collecting garment for resident

indicators.note: collecting means the first pieces gather the garment inside them

parts.note: in means fashionable, in favour
an ant is a worker insect
a habit is a nun's or monk's robe

explanation.surface: A favourite employee picks up clothing on behalf of someone living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' is the fashionable sense of in, as in the in crowd; 'collecting' wraps the robe inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who lives in a place, a dweller.

clue.text: Embarrassed performer? One may have changed the text

definitions.text: One may have changed the text

parts.note: red is how an embarrassed face looks
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A blushing actor whose lines were rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an editor, who revises or censors a text.

clue.text: One who will say prayers in correct order

indicators.note: in says the answer is lodged inside the following words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A churchman recites prayers in their proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct order' looks like an anagram signal; the letters sit there already in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a parish priest, who leads the prayers in church.
